chapter: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
title: Using song quotes related to the tune or setting
summary: Knowing lyrics affects his playing; he quotes songs that relate to the piece, such as New Orleans tunes when playing about New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Does it have a relationship to your playing, too? Would you play a song differently if you knew the lyrics than if you didn't?
I think you would. Because say you're playing something about the weather, you know. In your lip (?), you'd try to find some words...think of some song

that's got weather in it, like "Stormy Weather". Or suppose you're singing...oh, let me see; I'm trying to think of some song... That you will connect with. A song to connect with. Sometimes, if we were playing, like, in New Orleans, put "Way Down South In Dixie" in it, or something like that. You know...?

I will think about it, you know, and then put that in there. Or put "Way Down Yonder In New Orleans" or, if we're playing...you know, "Do You Know What It Means To Miss New Orleans"... You know, things like that. Something that relates. That's what I usually do. So that's the way it goes. That's the way I do it. I know a lot of people use other songs that don't relate at all to the piece, because they don't know the words nohow. You know, they can't think of the words to it.
